To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the stability range of the four-wave interaction in a medium where Brillouin scattering occurs depends on the boundary conditions, the initial amplitudes and phases of the waves, and the frequency detuning between the waves.

the solution of the system of equations describing four-wave interaction between optical and hypersound waves in a medium is stable under the boundary conditions corresponding to the four-wave phase-conugate mirror and the phase synchronizer, provided the initial values of the amplitudes and phases of the waves are within certain limits.

the system of equations for the four-wave mixing process in the medium with stimulated Brillouin interaction is stable under conditions of phase conjugation and synchronization of four light waves, and this stability is determined by the ratio of the amplitude of the pump wave and the amplitude of the wave of stimulated Brillouin backscattering, and the ratio of the phase shift between the pump wave and one of the waves of stimulated Brillouins backscattering and the wave of stimulated Raman scattering.
In summary, our research is concerned with
nonlinear optical effects in liquids and solids.
the study of the nonlinear optical properties of materials and devices for the generation and amplification of light waves.
the study of the nonlinear optical effects that occur when light waves interact in a medium where there are hypersound waves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the four-wave interaction is stable against amplitude, phase (in the case of a four-wave phase conjugate mirror), and polarization perturbions.
the system is unstable against amplitude perturbations and stable against phase and polarization perturbances.
the system is stable in the sense of small perturbations in the amplitude, phase, or polarization of the input light waves, provided that the input waves are not too intense.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stability conditions are very sensitive to the parameters of the medium.
the four-wave phase-conugate mirror is the most stable configuration, and that the phase synchronizer is the least stable.
the system is stable against perturbations in amplitude, phase, or polarization if the perturbation does not change the phase-matching condition.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the phase conjugate and the synchronizer configurations have a similar range of stability against amplitude perturbations, and that both of these configurations have a wider stability range than a conventional four-wave phase conjugator.
the system is more stable against amplitude perturbations than phase and polarization perturbances.
the system is stable under a broad range of conditions.
